summary_md: **W.Cheng ([@wchengphy](https://x.com/wchengphy/status/2116708185826295820))** summarizes *Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting* by Tan et al. ([arXiv 2610.20563](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20563)): research agents plateau as they anchor on past attempts, and periodically wiping history while keeping only the best candidate gave 39% better results than a single agent on AHC014 at the same budget.
relevance: Forgetting as a tool for agent discovery.

media.description: Two line charts versus dollars spent: AHC014 score (higher is better) and VLIW kernel cycles (lower is better), where a team of 4 agents with periodic forgetting beats 4 parallel agents and a single agent.
